name: PWE Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The belt at the top of PWE's Revenge brand, and the one its own paperwork keeps changing the name of: the front page called it the PWE World Championship in the spring of 2005 and the Heavyweight Championship by the autumn. Ryan Styles carried it out of Saga III in May and lost it in the main event of Deadly Game at Madison Square Garden on 27 November 2005, to Nicholas Pryde, by submission. Eddy Guerrero had challenged for it a month earlier and Sting a year before that; the fed's own record of who held it before Styles is not in the surviving record.

name: PWE Television Championship
epitaph: The belt PWE's own records call the longest-held in its history: The Regulator carried it 308 days, longer than any championship reign the fed ever counted. It was held by two men at once for a stretch of 2005, after Revenge's own authority figure named The Regulator and Alex Hoffman co-champions when both made the same opponent tap out in the same match. Homicide had it by the autumn and kept it against The Amityville Horror at Deadly Game.

name: PWE Iron Man Championship
epitaph: Defended, at least once, in the match it is named for: Lee Nolan took it off The Prototype three falls to nothing in a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Deadly Game 2005. Before that The Elite defended it in an Ultimate X match against three challengers at Saga III and lost it to one of them, Clarke "The X" Andrews, at The Reckoning that July.

name: PWE Undisputed Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Crowned out of a tournament whose final the Prodigal Sons reached at Last Man Standing on 28 August 2005, and defended in a tables, ladders and chairs match against Fight Against Prejudice at Deadly Game that November.

name: PWE Dream Championship
epitaph: Chaos held it through the spring of 2005 and kept it against Kurt Angle in a Weapon of Choice match at Annihilation. By Deadly Game that November the fed's own results page was calling the same belt the UCW Dream Championship, defended in a cage of weapons by Jarrell Young against three challengers; both names are the fed's own and neither is treated as a correction of the other.

name: PWE Pure Championship
epitaph: Jeff Jarrett beat Crunch for it at Annihilation in the spring of 2005, which is the only thing PWE's surviving paperwork says about the belt at all.

name: PWE Silver Crown
epitaph: Unified out of two belts and into one at Deadly Game 2005: Postal Maniac defended it against Christian and DisasterPiece in a three-way asylum match, won by grabbing both the Silver Crown and the WWE Intercontinental Championship at once, and the fed's own results say the two titles were unified there.

name: PWE Hardcore Championship
notes: The only appearance of the belt in the held record is the segment heading "Seg 9 – Hardcore Champion?!" and the sentence under it (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/underground-network-oct-10-milw-wi-2005-10-09.html).
epitaph: Named once in the surviving record, in the ninth segment of an Underground broadcast from the Bradley Center on 10 October 2005 that opens on a man holding the belt and a question mark in the segment's own title.

name: Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: PWE's own front-page results bill this belt, verbatim, as the “WWE Intercontinental Championship” — the fed's own paperwork borrowing a real promotion's real title name rather than inventing one of its own. It ends the only way the surviving record shows it: unified into the PWE Silver Crown when Postal Maniac grabbed both belts at once in a Three Way Asylum Match at Deadly Game 2005, beating co-champion Christian and DisasterPiece.
notes: Named exactly as the fed's own front page billed it — “WWE Intercontinental Championship” — kept here without the real-brand prefix per this registry's own title-naming convention; no other served document names it, and its own prior lineage is not in the surviving record.

events.title: pwe-inc-silver-crown
events.note: Postal Maniac grabbed both belts at once in a Three Way Asylum Match at Deadly Game 2005, unifying them (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/front-page-news-2005-12-05.html).

name: PWE World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: PWE Underground's own top belt — a second, brand-specific championship the surviving record never once shows crossing paths with Revenge's own Heavyweight/World Championship. Chaos carried it into Underground Network on 10 October 2005 and lost it there to Bulldozer, who won it with a sledgehammer shot once the referee was knocked cold; a community wrap-up column the next day corroborated the same result while airing a dispute over the two writers' own RP agreement. A departing champion's own promo names Kurt Angle, ZerO and Tex Graham himself among its past holders, alongside Deuce Jackson before Chaos — spoken evidence only, no dates or documents behind any of it.
notes: Distinct from pwe-inc-heavyweight (Revenge's own belt, Ryan Styles to Nicholas Pryde): the corpus stages what read as two parallel Heavyweight/World title lineages, one per brand, never shown unifying or resolving against each other in any served document. Kept separate rather than merged on guesswork — see the wing's own tier_source note.
